subject: what a ten-year projection can show
preheader: year one and a projection answer different questions.
headline: A ten-year projection makes long-run assumptions visible.
body: Year-one cash flow describes the entered first-year assumptions. A ten-year projection asks a different question: what those inputs would produce if the selected rent growth, expense growth, financing, appreciation, and selling-cost assumptions occurred. Neither is a forecast or a guarantee.

TrueCap starts rent growth and expense growth at editable 2.5% assumptions. Principal and interest stay fixed only for the modeled fixed-rate schedule; other costs and property performance can change differently from the assumptions.

Use the projection to inspect the effect of each input, then stress and replace it with evidence appropriate to the property. A precise year-ten result is still conditional on the assumptions that produced it.

The flip side is also true. A 'great' property with seller-financed assumable debt at 3.5% looks amazing in year one — but if the rent is already above market and the area is softening, year ten could be uglier than year one.

The 10-year projection and report are available when the current access rules include them. Custom branding requires an eligible paid plan. Review the pricing page for current plan availability, then treat every exported value as a modeled scenario for adviser or lender review—not as an approval or forecast.
